title: Elson.ai
description: A local-first macOS voice agent for dictation, cleanup, replies, and paste-first desktop work.
body:
Elson.ai is the voice layer I want on my own Mac: fast dictation, transcript cleanup, screenshot-aware replies, and a paste-first workflow that ends inside the app I am already using.

It is intentionally local-first and inspectable. Not another black-box assistant window. Elson sits closer to the desktop, listens when needed, cleans up messy human input, and gives me text that is ready to use. The product direction is simple: the Mac remains the workspace, Elson becomes the small assistant layer that catches speech, context, and intent without forcing every task into a chat UI.

## What it does

- Turns speech into usable writing for chat, docs, email, coding notes, and daily desktop work.
- Cleans rough transcripts into text that sounds like a person, not a recorder dump.
- Uses screenshot context for lightweight replies and better situational help.
- Keeps the flow paste-first so the assistant does not become the workspace.
- Treats permissions, app context, clipboard flow, and fast correction as core product details.
- Keeps distribution practical with release artifacts that people can install instead of a demo that only runs on one machine.

## Why this project exists

Most voice tools either stop at transcription or become a heavy assistant surface that wants to own the whole interaction. Elson sits in the middle. The useful loop is not just “speech to text”; it is speech, cleanup, optional context, intent, correction, and a final result that can be pasted wherever the real work happens.

That makes the product feel closer to a desktop utility than a chatbot. It should help with the small moments where typing is slow: turning a rough thought into a Slack reply, rewriting a dictated note, responding with screen context, or capturing a messy idea before it disappears.

## Recent work from local commits

The newer commits are very product-heavy. Elson gained persisted audio captures, menu copy buttons, chunked recording, recording-state refinements, lower-energy audio forwarding into ASR, screenshot-context optimization, post-response word correction, and refreshed distribution artifacts.

The 0.0.44 release work shipped modern and compatibility DMGs plus the universal installer. A later README pass sharpened the positioning around Elson as an open-source Wispr-style Mac voice assistant.

On May 19 the app architecture was simplified around explicit shortcut routing. The feedback-learning layer and stale history-summary helpers were removed, shortcut intent reduction became test-covered, skill selection was filtered into its own path, and conversation history titles moved directly into the primary prompt output. The result is a cleaner local agent loop: less hidden correction state, clearer keyboard behavior, and more predictable prompt context.

## Product decisions

Elson is built around a few constraints that matter in practice. It should be fast enough to use mid-thought. It should expose what it can and cannot see. It should make the output easy to copy or paste. It should avoid a giant “assistant cockpit” when a small utility action is enough. And it should keep the desktop environment as the first-class surface.

The shortcut-routing cleanup is part of that philosophy. A voice assistant becomes frustrating when keyboard behavior feels magical or when hidden feedback state changes future outputs in ways the user cannot inspect. Making intent routing explicit gives the app a firmer foundation for more actions later.

## Current direction

The next useful direction is less about adding another model call and more about making the loop reliable: clearer capture states, better correction, safer prompt context, stronger release packaging, and enough local structure that the app can grow without turning into spaghetti.

## Public boundary

This page describes the public app surface, release artifacts, and product workflow. It does not expose private recordings, local user data, credentials, or unreleased account details.
